modules.title: The Precise Definition of a Limit

alg_eval.description: Uses the wrong piece of a piecewise function for the given input (ignores the condition on x).
Order-of-operations or sign error when substituting, e.g. -2^2 evaluated as 4 or 3(-1)^2 as -3.
Treats an undefined value (division by zero) as 0 instead of undefined.

alg_slope.description: Computes run over rise, (x2 - x1)/(y2 - y1), instead of rise over run.
Subtracts in inconsistent order, (y2 - y1)/(x1 - x2), giving the wrong sign.

alg_factor.description: Sign error in a factor, e.g. x^2 - x - 6 = (x + 3)(x - 2).
Factors a sum of squares as if it were a difference, e.g. x^2 + 4 = (x - 2)(x + 2).
Misremembers the sum/difference of cubes pattern, e.g. x^3 - 8 = (x - 2)(x^2 + 4).

alg_rational.description: Cancels terms rather than factors, e.g. (x^2 - 4)/(x - 2) -> x - 2 by cancelling x with x^2 or (x + 3)/x -> 3.
Treats the simplified expression as identical to the original, including at the excluded point.

alg_conjugate.description: Multiplies only the numerator (or only the denominator) by the conjugate, changing the value.
Expands (sqrt(a) - b)(sqrt(a) + b) incorrectly, e.g. as a - b instead of a - b^2.
Splits a square root over a sum: sqrt(a + b) = sqrt(a) + sqrt(b).

alg_complex_fraction.description: Adds fractions by adding numerators and denominators: 1/a + 1/b = 2/(a + b).
Inverts the wrong fraction or drops the outer denominator when clearing a complex fraction.

alg_abs.description: Drops absolute-value bars, treating |x - a| as x - a on both sides of a.
Distributes absolute value over a sum: |x - a| = |x| - |a|.

alg_domain.description: Finds where the function is undefined from the simplified form, missing points removed by cancelling.
Treats zeros of the numerator as points where the function is undefined.

alg_sign.description: Loses track of sign through an even power, e.g. thinks (x - 2)^2 is negative for x < 2.
Uses the sign from the wrong side of the point (e.g. x - a > 0 for x slightly less than a).

alg_abs_ineq.description: Solves |x - a| < d as x - a < d only, missing the lower bound.
Mishandles a constant factor, e.g. |3x - 6| < e read as |x - 2| < e instead of |x - 2| < e/3.

trig_values.description: Swaps sine and cosine values at special angles (e.g. sin(pi/6) = sqrt(3)/2).
Treats a radian input as degrees (or vice versa).
Wrong sign for a trig value outside the first quadrant.

trig_identities.description: Misuses the Pythagorean identity, e.g. 1 - cos^2 x = sin x or sin^2 x + cos^2 x = 0.
Cancels inside a trig function, e.g. sin(2x)/x = sin 2 or sin(x)/x = sin.

secant_slope.description: Treats a single secant slope as the exact tangent slope rather than an approximation that improves as x approaches a.
Uses the wrong pair of points (e.g. (a, f(x)) and (x, f(a))).

avg_velocity.description: Averages two velocities or positions instead of dividing displacement by elapsed time.
Reports a position (or displacement) as the velocity.

area_rectangles.description: Uses left endpoints when right endpoints were asked (or vice versa).
Adds heights without multiplying by the rectangle width.

limit_intuitive.description: Thinks the limit at a must equal f(a), or uses f(a) when it differs from the nearby values.

source.text: A function has to be continuous at x=a if the lim_(x→a) f(x) exists.

limit_intuitive.description: Thinks that if f(a) is undefined then the limit cannot exist.

source.text: If there is a vertical asymptote at x=a for the function f(x), then f is undefined at the point x=a.

limit_intuitive.description: Thinks the function must actually reach the limit value.

limit_table.description: Uses values from only one side of a when estimating a two-sided limit.
Reports the last table entry verbatim instead of the value the entries approach.

limit_graph.description: Reads the filled dot (the function value) as the limit instead of where the curve heads.
Reads the left piece for a right-hand limit or vice versa.

one_sided.description: Swaps left- and right-hand limits (x -> a^- read as from the right).
Uses f(a) for a one-sided limit when the function value differs.

limit_existence.description: Says the two-sided limit exists because one one-sided limit exists.
Averages unequal one-sided limits to get a two-sided limit.

infinite_limits.description: Gets the sign of an infinite limit wrong (+infinity vs -infinity).
Treats infinity as a number that the limit equals in the ordinary sense (e.g. says the limit exists and equals infinity, then does arithmetic with it).

vertical_asymptote.description: Puts a vertical asymptote where the factor cancels (a removable point).

source.text: If there is a vertical asymptote at x=a for the function f(x), then f is undefined at the point x=a.

vertical_asymptote.description: Puts a vertical asymptote at a zero of the numerator.

limit_laws.description: Applies the quotient law when the limit of the denominator is 0.

source.text: You can use the quotient rule to evaluate lim_(x→0) (sin x)/(x). False

limit_laws.description: Misapplies a law, e.g. lim(f g) = lim f + lim g, or applies a law to limits that do not exist.

direct_substitution.description: Stops at 0/0 and reports the limit as 0, 1, or 'does not exist' without further work.

factor_cancel.description: Declares the limit 0, 1, or DNE on seeing 0/0 instead of simplifying.
Cancels correctly but reports an expression, or substitutes into the original form again.

conjugate_limit.description: Multiplies only one part by the conjugate.
Declares the limit 0, 1, or DNE on seeing 0/0 instead of rationalizing.

complex_fraction_limit.description: Adds fractions across numerators and denominators.
Declares the limit 0, 1, or DNE on seeing 0/0 instead of simplifying.
Sign error when combining over a common denominator (e.g. a - x vs x - a).

nonzero_over_zero.description: Declares +infinity (or DNE) without checking the sign on each side.
Wrong sign on one side of the point.

piecewise_limits.description: Uses the wrong piece for a one-sided limit.
Uses the function value at the boundary instead of the one-sided limits.
Concludes the limit exists because the function is defined at the point.

squeeze.description: Uses bounding functions whose limits are not equal and still concludes a limit.
Claims sin(1/x) (or cos(1/x)) itself tends to 0, or drops the oscillating factor.
Writes an incorrect bound (e.g. -1 <= x sin(1/x) <= 1 used as if it proved the limit).

trig_limits.description: Cancels x inside the sine: sin(kx)/x = sin k.
Forgets the rescaling factor, e.g. lim sin(3x)/x = 1 instead of 3.

continuity_point.description: Checks only that f(a) is defined (or only that the limit exists), not all three conditions.
Assumes lim f = f(a) without computing the limit.

discontinuity_types.description: Calls a cancelling factor an infinite discontinuity, or a non-cancelling one removable.

continuity_interval.description: Includes a point where the function is undefined in an interval of continuity.
Uses closed brackets at an excluded endpoint or open brackets where one-sided continuity holds.

continuity_parameter.description: Sets the wrong pieces equal, or evaluates the pieces at the wrong point.
Sets up the right equation but solves it incorrectly.

composite_continuity.description: Moves the limit inside a function that is not continuous at the inner limit.
Correct method but wrong exact trig value.

ivt.description: Applies the IVT to a function that is not continuous on the closed interval.

source.text: According to the IVT, cos x-sin x-x=2 has a solution over the interval [−1,1].

ivt.description: Concludes no zero exists because f(a) and f(b) have the same sign.
Claims the IVT gives the location or number of zeros.

epsilon_delta_def.description: Reverses the roles of epsilon and delta (chooses epsilon given delta).
Omits the 0 < |x - a| condition or the strictness of the inequalities.

epsilon_delta_linear.description: Takes delta = epsilon regardless of the slope.
Multiplies by the slope instead of dividing (delta = m * epsilon).

epsilon_delta_nonlinear.description: Leaves |x + a| unbounded (no preliminary restriction such as delta <= 1).
Forgets to take the minimum of the two restrictions on delta.
